Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `HexDumpTest.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/local_workplace/commons-io/src/test/java/org/apache/commons/io/HexDumpTest.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

I've read both files. The original test is functionally fine but has understandability issues: the `testDumpOutputStream` method has three nearly-identical ~30-line blocks that manually build expected byte arrays with the magic number `73`, cryptic `j`/`k` loop variables, and repeated assertion loops. Let me refactor for clarity while preserving exact behavior.Now let me compile-check the refactored test.The refactored `HexDumpTest.java` compiles successfully (`COMPILE_OK`). I improved understandability by extracting named constants (`DATA_SIZE`, `BYTES_PER_LINE`, `LINE_TEXT_LENGTH`, `LINE_WIDTH` with a documented derivation of the former magic number 73), replacing the three duplicated ~30-line expected-output blocks with reusable, well-named helpers (`createSequentialData`, `dumpToBytes`, `expectedFullDump`, `expectedDumpFromIndex0x81`, `assertDumpEquals`), renaming cryptic `j`/`k` loops to `line`/`col`, and adding explanatory comments — all while calling the same `HexDump` methods with the same arguments and producing identical expected outcomes.
